comment: The Question. Dr. Chen. Timed to spoken lines.

lines.text: Dr. Chen has taught Network Protocols for eleven years. He wrote the textbook. He knows this stuff cold.
But every semester, there's that one student.
Dr. Chen, in Week 4 you said TCP uses three-way handshake. But RFC 8312 mentions a two-way variant for constrained devices. Why don't we cover that?
He has no idea. It's not in the lecture notes. It's not in the curriculum. It's not even in his textbook.
And forty students are watching him flip.
But this semester, Chen has MeetHint.
Great question, Jessica. RFC 8312 defines a two-way handshake for constrained IoT devices.
It's outside our standard curriculum, but if you're interested, I have supplementary reading — page 8.
Dr. Chen, will this be on the final?
That's not in our current material. I'll confirm and email the class by Friday.
If it's not in his files, MeetHint stays empty. No guessing. No BS. Cite or silence.
When the lecture ends, he doesn't have a transcript. He has an audit.
Every claim checked. Every gap flagged. Every student question he couldn't answer — tracked for next semester.
Whatever you get asked about — lectures, contracts, code, curriculum — MeetHint lives in your browser. Nothing uploads. Nothing leaks.
It just finds the exact line, so you say what the file says, not what you hope is true.
Stop flipping. Stop guessing. Stop hoping nobody asks the one thing you can't find.
Your files are the source of truth. The meeting just became searchable.
MeetHint AI. Cite or silence.
Forty students are watching. Then someone asks the thing that isn't in the lecture.
MeetHint pulls the line from his files. Nothing uploaded.
If it's not in the pack, the card stays empty.
Cite or silence.
